# The reasons

The most remarkable chapter of the 1446 book is the one that explains *why*: why
ㄱ (*g*) is shaped like the back of the tongue blocking the throat, why the
vowels build from three primitives. That chapter was lost for five hundred
years, so the world had the letters but not the reasons. A surviving copy came
to light in 1940. The letters worked the whole time. But a system whose reasons
are lost cannot be extended, only used.

This part is gog's reasons, published with the package on purpose. It states the
nine laws the package never breaks, and the one shortcut they all exist to
refuse. It says why the engine refuses what it refuses, and why every refusal
comes with a direction. None of it is required to *use* gog. The earlier parts
cite these laws by name, and never ask you to have read them. It is here for the
moment you want to know why the grammar is shaped the way it is. It also
predicts what the engine will do in a case no chapter covers.

The laws all refuse the same thing, and it has a name: the expert's
shortcut, the saved keystroke that takes a rule away from the beginner.
